summary.intent: Investigate and fix someguy IPNS routing failures on staging, implement a delegated-ipfs.dev fallback with Prometheus metrics, and resolve a long-standing release-please tagging deadlock that prevented automated releases.
summary.outcome: Someguy was fixed (libp2p port, DHT mode, resource limits), fallback routing with metrics was implemented and tested, all E2E tests pass. The release-please deadlock was traced to old staging tags (v*-staging*) colliding with the root package scanner, and ultimately to include-component-in-tag: false being broken in multi-package mode; switched to cipher-box-v* tag format.

repo: Someguy's SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY env var expects raw uint64 bytes, not human-readable strings like '1GB' — causes crash loop on startup.
The DelegatedRoutingClient uses fire-and-forget IPNS publish; DB is always ahead of DHT so 100% of IPNS resolves are served from the database, not the network.

release-please with the Merge plugin generates PRs titled 'chore: release main' (not 'chore: release v${version}'), but the real blocker was include-component-in-tag: false being broken in multi-package mode — the release scanner cannot match bare v{version} tags back to the root path.
Old staging releases (v*-staging-rc-*) were being parsed by release-please as component 'staging' with version 'rc-1', polluting the release scanner and causing 'Missing 1 paths: .' failures.

release-please deadlocks with 'untagged, merged release PRs outstanding' when a merged release PR has autorelease: pending but the tag was never created — must manually create the tag AND flip label to autorelease: tagged to unblock.
Vitest does NOT auto-load .env files into process.env — env vars must be passed explicitly via CLI (e.g. THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET=x pnpm exec vitest) or configured in vitest.config.ts.
The API's throttler bypass uses an x-throttle-bypass header with a secret, not NODE_ENV detection.
Someguy self-hosted has higher median latency than delegated-ipfs.dev (~20-70% slower p50) but better tail latency (p99 ~20% lower) due to no CDN variability.
The mock-ipns-routing service should be kept for CI (instant, no DHT warmup, no outbound internet needed) even though someguy handles local dev.

code.finding: resolveRecord() tries delegated routing first but always also queries DB; if both return results, higher sequence number wins. Since DB is written synchronously before DHT publish (which is fire-and-forget), DB always has higher seq number and 100% of resolves are DB-served.
backend parameter typed as 'primary' | 'fallback' literal union — PR review caught it was typed as string, fixed to union type.
Throttler bypass uses x-throttle-bypass header + THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET env var, not NODE_ENV=test. Tests need THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET set and sent as a default header via SDK client.

workflow: release-please in multi-package mode requires include-component-in-tag: true with an explicit component name for the root package; bare v{version} tags are not reliably matched back to the root path.

When release-please fails to tag a merged release PR, the fix requires: (1) manually create the missing git tag + GitHub Release, (2) flip label from autorelease: pending to autorelease: tagged, (3) re-run the workflow.

Staging pre-release GitHub Releases must use a format release-please cannot parse as a component — prefix-based format (staging-v0.26.2-rc-1) still gets parsed as component 'staging'; consider not creating GitHub Releases for staging builds at all.
Docker healthcheck commands run inside the container — wget vs curl availability must be verified inside the container image (docker exec ... which wget), not on the host.
SSH root access to staging VPS is available via 1Password agent SSH key, separate from the CI deploy key which only works from GitHub Actions runner IPs.

friction: release-please deadlock saga consumed the majority of the session — the root cause (include-component-in-tag: false broken in multi-package mode) was only discovered after exhausting: title pattern fixes, bootstrap-sha, label resets, staging tag format changes, component: '' empty string, and manually anchoring releases.
Old staging releases (v*-staging-rc-*) had to be manually deleted en masse (29 releases) — they were never cleaned up and caused release-please scanner noise.
vitest not auto-loading .env files caused initial 429 failures that looked like throttling bugs, wasted debugging time.
SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY crash loop was only discovered post-deploy by SSHing into the staging VPS — no local indication it would fail.
Web E2E tests on main were flaky and blocked auto-merge on multiple release PRs, requiring manual re-runs.
GitHub API race condition caused release-please to fail adding autorelease: pending label to a freshly created PR (node ID not yet resolved).
Git stash on branch switch silently dropped file edits, requiring the changes to be redone on the new branch.
open_items: packages/crypto is now in release-please config but its first auto-managed release will bump to 0.26.0 based on accumulated history — version alignment with the rest of the monorepo is not clean.
Staging desktop builds create GitHub Releases that release-please scans — these may continue to interfere with the release scanner even with the new cipher-box-v* tag format for the root package.
DB-first IPNS resolution means 100% of resolves hit the database — if DB load becomes an issue, the lever is to prefer network result when sequence numbers match.
The mock-ipns-routing service is redundant for local dev now that someguy runs locally — left in place for now, could be removed from docker-compose.yml in a future cleanup.
Someguy SOMEGUY_IPNS_ENDPOINTS fanout config (race vs fallback) was investigated but not implemented — the API-level fallback is in place instead; the sidecar-level config remains default.
Grafana alert rules for cipherbox_delegated_routing_fallbacks_total were not configured — only the metric was added; alert setup is deferred.
Release-please anchor release for packages/crypto was created at v0.25.1 on the current HEAD commit rather than at the actual historical commit where 0.25.1 was released.
